newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek fixed coupon bonds rally, ecu/drachma ranges.
newsitem.headline: Greek fixed coupon bonds rally, ecu/drachma ranges.

text.p: Greek fixed coupon bonds were rallying, ecu/drachma was rangebound in the tight 309.60/80 band, depos were softer from six-month to 12-month periods, forex forwards were steady to firmer in short tenors, dealers said.
"Bonds, especially three-and five-year fixed coupon bonds, rally," said a senior bond trader at a private bank. "Bond prices are up 30 to 50 basis points since Thursday."
The market outlook for lower interest rates in the next few months coupled with a reduced supply of FRNs were the driving forces behind the surge in bond prices, dealers said.
"The market is convinced that the ministry has shifted away from auctioning FRNs to fixed coupon bonds," the trader said.
Greece will issue 4.0 percent, five-and 10-year CPI-indexed bonds on May 19 and 12-month T-bills at a single-digit rate on June 2, said deputy Finance Minister Nickos Christodoulakis on Thursday.
The treasury will also auction about 150 billion drachmas of 10-year fixed coupon bonds in mid-June, the minister said.
Consumer price inflation eased to 5.9 percent year-on-year in April from 6.0 percent in March, the National Statistics Service (NSS) said in a statement.
Depos were softer about five basis points from six-to 12-months and short-term forex forwards were slightly up, dealers said.
The mark was quoted at 159.07/12 from Thursday's 159.070 fix, the dollar at 271.21/31 drachmas from 272.300 and the ecu at 309.73/83 from 309.600 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is locked in the 309.60/80 range this morning," said a forex trader at a foreign bank.
